what: XP is a Brazilian financial services firm. It built an investment platform that broke the grip of Brazil's large banks on retail investing, distributing funds, equities, fixed income and pension products through its own advisers and an affiliated network of independent agents. It has since added banking, cards and insurance.
customers: Brazilian retail investors, from first-time savers to high-net-worth clients, plus corporate clients using its investment banking and treasury services.
money: Commissions and fees on investment products distributed to individual clients.
Trading, investment banking and corporate services.
Credit cards, lending, insurance and pension products.
moat: Its network of thousands of affiliated independent advisers is the real asset: those advisers own the client relationships and bring them to XP's platform, which the incumbent banks cannot easily replicate. Brazilian savers moving money out of bank deposits into market products has been a structural shift, and XP has been its main beneficiary.
risks: Brazilian interest rates are high, and when fixed-income deposits pay well, investors are less inclined to buy the higher-fee products XP earns most from.
Reported revenue figures move with both accounting basis and the Brazilian real, so year-to-year comparisons in US dollars can be misleading.
The large Brazilian banks have built competing digital investment platforms and are willing to cut fees.
Brazilian political and currency risk affects both the business and the value of its earnings to a dollar investor.
Growth in client assets has slowed considerably from the pace of several years ago.
opportunities: The shares trade at about 6.9 times earnings, a low multiple for a platform business with roughly $903.9M of net income.
Cash of about $2.1B against $269.4M of debt gives a strong position.
Brazilian household savings are still heavily concentrated in bank deposits, so the shift toward market products has far to run.
Twelve analysts average a $19.94 target, about 46% above the current price.
watch: Net new money from clients. Market values move assets up and down on their own; net inflows show whether XP is still winning clients from the banks, which is the whole thesis.
